public_rationale: Part of the claim holds. CNET quietly published AI-written stories and, after an audit, corrected 41 of the 77, so 'a lot' of mistakes is accurate. But Marcus tied this to faith in ChatGPT and called them 'ChatGPT-written stories'. CNET's editor-in-chief said the stories were made with an internally designed AI engine, 'not ChatGPT'. The many-errors part is supported; the ChatGPT attribution is contradicted. A loose reading of 'ChatGPT' as shorthand for ChatGPT-style AI would weaken the contradiction, but the adjacent sentence names ChatGPT directly. 'First casualty' is rhetorical and was not scored.
limitations: The ChatGPT denial comes from CNET itself, and the underlying model was not disclosed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: CNET was the first casualty of putting too much faith in ChatGPT, publishing AI-written stories with many mistakes.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Reports show the stories had few or no errors, or that the tool was not ChatGPT.
